ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an aromatic ring with an NO2 substituent and a Se anion substituent; on the right side is connected a carbon chain containing an R substituent, and it is connected to an oxygen atom and a PBu3 cation fragment; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: Count according to bonds between heavy atoms, not counting hydrogen-related bonds. In the left aryl/nitro/selenium fragment, the benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds, there is 1 C-N bond between the benzene ring and NO2, there are 2 N-O bonds in NO2, and there is 1 C-Se bond between the benzene ring and Se, for a total of 10. In the visible chain segment on the right, when not including the interior of the butyl groups, there are R-C, C-C, C-O, and O-P, 4 bonds in total. PBu3 represents three butyl groups; each butyl group contains 1 P-C bond and 3 C-C bonds, namely 4 bonds per butyl group, and the three butyl groups have 12 bonds in total. The total is 10 + 4 + 12 = 26.

method.method_draft: Segment the image and tally heavy-atom bonds. Left aryl/nitro/selenide fragment: benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds, the ring-NO2 attachment has 1 C-N bond, NO2 has 2 N-O bonds, and the aryl-Se bond has 1, giving 10. Right visible chain excluding the butyl internals: R-C, C-C, C-O, and O-P give 4. PBu3 contributes three butyl groups, each with P-C plus three C-C bonds = 4 bonds, so 12 total. Add 10 + 4 + 12 = 26.

method.method_draft: Count heavy graph nodes and cycles. Left component: 6 aryl carbons + N + 2 O + Se = 10 nodes, with one benzene cycle.
